subject.title: [Bug]: Subagent completion silently lost — no retry, no notification, no auto-restart on timeout

question: Should OpenClaw make subagent completion delivery a durable at-least-once parent-session contract with visible terminal failure, or keep bounded best-effort announce semantics with clearer task/operator visibility?
rationale: The source path is clear, but the permanent behavior affects session semantics, duplicate-delivery risk, retry policy, task audit state, and user-visible channel delivery, so automation should not choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Durable Completion Recovery
options.body: Treat the completion result as durable pending work until the requester processes it or a visible terminal blocked state is recorded, with duplicate suppression and channel proof before closure.

options.title: Failure Visibility Only
options.body: Keep bounded announce retries but require task audit, session status, and requester/operator notification to make give-up visible without promising at-least-once delivery.

options.title: Document Best Effort
options.body: Accept current best-effort semantics, close broad reliability work, and keep only narrower bugs such as queue ACK or timeout warning reports open.

recommendation.title: Durable Completion Recovery
recommendation.body: Treat the completion result as durable pending work until the requester processes it or a visible terminal blocked state is recorded, with duplicate suppression and channel proof before closure.

likelyOwner.reason: The current-main retry/give-up implementation and docs are primarily on steipete-authored recent commits, and this is a cross-surface product contract choice.
